title: Multiplexed micro-lane token pacing for rerank to reduce tail latency
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: The public reranking endpoint shows sporadic 95th/99th latency spikes under mixed-length traffic and heavy embedding-prefetch loads. Current monolithic microbatching and single-slot KV prefetch create head-of-line blocking when long-token candidates or cold KV lookups enter a batch.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight multiplexed micro-lane scheduler that partitions incoming rerank requests into small ‘‘micro-lanes’’ by estimated token cost and KV-prefetch state. Each lane has its own pacing token budget and deadline-aware admission rules so short candidates can bypass long ones. The scheduler combines parallel lane execution across available workers and enforces per-lane soft timeouts and graceful early-exit to keep tail latency bounded.

Goals: 1) Reduce 95th/99th latency by 25-40% for rerank workloads with mixed candidate lengths. 2) Maintain or improve overall throughput and cost per scored candidate. 3) Keep quality unchanged: no more than 0.5% regression in canonical eval metrics across our rerank test set.
acceptance_criteria: 95th latency improvement >= 25% on mixed-length synthetic benchmark compared to baseline microbatch scheduler
99th latency improvement >= 20% without dropping mean throughput by >10%
No regression >0.5% on NDCG@10 and MRR evals on canonical rerank suite
End-to-end integration test for graceful early-exit that verifies fallback scoring path and monotonic score stability
Runbook updated with new metrics and SLO thresholds
implementation_plan: Design: define lane classification heuristics (estimated token count, has_kv_cached boolean, priority header)
Prototype: add micro-lane scheduler in rerank front-tier as opt-in feature flag (config via route settings)
Execution: implement per-lane pacing token bucket and deadline-aware admission that converts to worker microbatches
KV-prefetch coordination: surface has_kv_cached to scheduler, kick cold-KV candidates into low-parallelism lane with prefetch hints
Early-exit: implement soft-timeout that returns best-so-far scores for candidates not completed by lane deadline; add deterministic tie-breaker
Observability: emit per-lane latency histograms, lane drop rates, early-exit counts, and per-route cost delta
Rollout: staged canary on 5% of rerank traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on latency or quality regressions
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Design sync completed with infra and runtime teams. Agreed on lane keys: token_estimate_bucket and kv_state. Recorded design doc link.
2026-03-04: Prototype scheduler added behind feature flag. End-to-end flow validated in local harness with synthetic requests.
2026-03-08: Benchmarked prototype on m60 dev cluster. Observed 30% reduction in 95th under mixed-length workload but 8% drop in throughput; investigating batching efficiency tradeoffs.

2026-03-11: Implemented lightweight lane-coalescing to merge small lanes to improve throughput; re-benchmarks show throughput recovered to within 4% of baseline and 95th latency improvement maintained.
2026-03-12: Integration tests added for early-exit semantics and fallback scoring. Preparing canary config and SLO alarms. PRs opened (see links).
comments: Maya Chen (PM) 2026-03-03: Nice approach — please include a conservative default config for Dedicated customers so we don't alter committed latency guarantees.
Liam O'Connor (Runtime) 2026-03-05: Be careful exposing has_kv_cached; we should derive from prefetch metadata to avoid extra RTTs. Also ensure lane metadata is compact to not bloat request headers.
Priya Kapoor (Creator) 2026-03-07: Noted. We'll use existing prefetch response flags and extend the route config to set lane thresholds per-tenant.
Eve Thompson (SRE) 2026-03-09: Add a circuit-breaker for lane scheduler backpressure; on worker pressure, the scheduler should fall back to current microbatch behavior to avoid headroom exhaustion.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lane assignment heuristics and pacing token bucket
Integration test with KV prefetch mock to validate lane selection for warm vs cold lookups
Load tests on dev cluster with mixed-length traffic (short:1-8 tokens, medium:20-80, long:>200) measuring p50/p95/p99 and throughput
A/B canary against production rerank route for 2 weeks with continuous quality eval on production prompts
Chaos test: simulate worker loss and verify fallback to baseline microbatch and zero negative customer impact
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per route and per lane
throughput (scored candidates/sec) and cost per scored candidate
early-exit rate and average score delta for early-exit responses
lane occupancy, queueing time, and prefetch hit-rate
SLO breaches and automatic rollback triggers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased implementation complexity could introduce subtle bugs in ordering semantics. Mitigation: add determinism tests and maintain strict unit test coverage for ordering and tie-breakers.

Risk: Excessive lane fragmentation reduces batching efficiency and increases GPU overhead. Mitigation: implement lane-coalescing heuristics and dynamic threshold tuning based on observed latency/throughput.

Risk: Early-exit may degrade result quality for some customers. Mitigation: opt-in per-route, expose knobs to tune deadline and quality targets, and run continuous evals against representative prompt sets.
Risk: Interaction with Dedicated capacity SLAs. Mitigation: conservative default configs for Dedicated customers and release toggle behind enterprise feature flag.
